decision.name: Economic-dependency settlement guard and Gate B Golden impact
decision.dependency_rule: Block an Expense create/edit/delete when the current state or proposed post-state would change financial truth on which any unresolved settlement depends.
decision.create: Allow only when the proposed new Expense is economically independent of every unresolved settlement dependency.
decision.edit: Allow only when both the current Expense state and proposed post-state are economically independent of every unresolved settlement dependency.
decision.delete: Allow only when the current Expense state is economically independent of every unresolved settlement dependency.
decision.dispute_rule: Raising an issue remains allowed, but any prepared PaymentIntent depending on that Expense becomes invalid for execution and must be re-resolved.
decision.fail_closed_rule: For guarded mutations, unresolved settlement input is treated as locked unless the caller supplies authoritative evidence that the relevant scope is safely terminal or no-effect.
decision.unknown_effect_precedence: unknown_effect takes precedence over a terminal label until reconciliation establishes authoritative terminal/no-effect truth.
decision.partial_rule: A partial close does not release source dependency while an open remainder still references that lineage.
decision.explanation_rule: A blocked mutation must identify the settlement/dependency that caused the block.
decision.closeout_rule: Whole-group closeout remains an approved future semantic mode, but it is outside Gate B until a dedicated user path is separately approved.

golden_impact.rule: The approved locked recovery state remains reachable in Gate B when an attempted Expense mutation is blocked because it would change an unresolved settlement dependency.

The historical blanket-unavailable Add Expense behavior is superseded for ordinary settlements. Preserve it as historical Golden evidence and revisit it when a dedicated whole-group closeout surface is designed.

rationale: The user-approved principle is to lock whatever could invalidate an active settlement, no more and no less.
Frozen J11 states that the amount cannot exceed the current eligible balance, disputed source items are ineligible, and partial remainder preserves source lineage.
A source-id-only test is therefore insufficient: an otherwise unrelated mutation can become economically dependent through payer/participant/currency changes or eligible-balance drift.
Gate B should not invent a whole-group closeout control that has no approved Golden surface.
authority_note: This clarification is a new human product decision made after the frozen Golden baseline and after DEC-EXPENSE-SETTLEMENT-LOCK-01. It records the approved integration interpretation and its impact on historical J05/J08 settlement-lock states.
